rationale: Both prior blocking findings are resolved in the current source: the portal's Reorder at field now holds the raw text and converts to a number only on submit, so a cleared field stays blank and required blocks the save (CR-001), and a PATCH /tomes/1 rejection test covers -1, 1.5 and 3000000000 with a re-read confirming the level is unchanged (CR-002). Business and standards rows carried forward from the final round; running the suite, lint, typecheck and build remains Stage 7 evidence.

findings.title: Cleared reorder field silently saves level 0
findings.problem: The new 'Reorder at' input uses onChange={(e) => set({ reorderLevel: Number(e.target.value) })}. When the owner clears the field, Number('') coerces to 0, so form state holds 0 while the field shows blank; the required attribute never fires because the controlled value is 0, not empty.
findings.impact: An owner who clears the field and saves stores a reorder level of 0 without meaning to, so that tome only appears on the counter's Running low panel once it is completely sold out, defeating the feature's purpose for that tome.
findings.recommendation: Do not coerce an empty 'Reorder at' value to 0. Keep the field's raw string in form state (convert with Number only on submit) so the required attribute blocks a blank submit, or ignore empty input, e.g. onChange={(e) => set({ reorderLevel: e.target.value === '' ? form.reorderLevel : Number(e.target.value) })}. Make sure a deliberately typed 0 still saves as 0.
findings.check_notes: Tomes.tsx:208/274 keeps reorderLevel as a string; Number() applied only on submit (line 217), so a cleared field stays blank and required blocks the save; typed 0 still saves as 0.

fix.change: TomeDialog keeps reorderLevel as text while typing and converts with Number only on submit, so a cleared field stays blank and required blocks the save; a typed 0 still saves as 0

findings.title: PATCH never tested rejecting bad reorder levels
findings.problem: The rejection test it.each([-1, 1.5, 3000000000]) only sends invalid reorderLevel values through POST /tomes. PATCH /tomes/:id parses with the separate tomeChanges schema (tomeFields.omit({stock}).partial()) and no test sends an invalid value through it, although AC2 requires edits to reject them with 400 and AC8 requires the tests to cover AC2.
findings.impact: A regression in the edit schema (e.g. a later change to tomeChanges) could let an owner store a negative or fractional reorder level through the edit dialog without any test failing; the database CHECK would then surface it as a 500 rather than a clean 400.
findings.recommendation: Add a PATCH counterpart to the it.each([-1, 1.5, 3000000000]) rejection test: PATCH /tomes/1 as owner with each invalid reorderLevel must return 400, and a follow-up GET must show the level unchanged.
findings.check_notes: catalog.test.ts:126 adds it.each([-1, 1.5, 3000000000]) PATCH /tomes/1 as owner expecting 400, then GET confirms reorderLevel still 2 (beforeEach reseeds).
